html:
King of the Achaemenid Persian Empire from 486 to 465 BCE, son of Darius the Great. He is best known for his invasion of Greece in 480 BCE.

He first crushed revolts in Egypt and Babylonia. Then he took up his father's war on Greece with one of the largest armies of the ancient world. His engineers bridged the Hellespont with boats and cut a canal through the Athos peninsula. He broke through at the Battle of Thermopylae, where the Spartan king Leonidas died, and burned Athens. But the Greek fleet led by Themistocles destroyed his navy at the Battle of Salamis, and he went home. The army he left behind lost at the Battle of Plataea in 479 BCE.

At home he finished much of Persepolis. He was murdered by courtiers in 465 BCE. Most of what we know of his war comes from Herodotus. He is usually identified with King Ahasuerus of the biblical Book of Esther.
sum: King of the Achaemenid Persian Empire from 486 to 465 BCE, son of Darius the Great. He is best known for his invasion of Greece in 480 BCE.
